full_caption: Bertram Grimsby-Hale, Appellant, v. Horatio Yarborough, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Bertram Grimsby-Hale, the association governing the Stonebrook subdivision, brought this action to enjoin Horatio Yarborough from maintaining a detached structure at 1273 Ferndale Road, Lindenmere, KS in violation of Article IV of the recorded declaration.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The association waived enforcement as to fence height by failing to act against 3 comparable violations over a period of 20 years. Selective enforcement of a covenant against one owner, after acquiescence in like violations by others, is inequitable.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The business judgment rule shields the board's maintenance and budgeting decisions from judicial second-guessing where the board acted within its authority, on an informed basis, and in the honest belief that the action served the association.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Article IV prohibits 'any outbuilding, shed or accessory structure exceeding one hundred twenty square feet.' The structure erected by Horatio Yarborough measures 660 square feet and is therefore within the plain reach of the restriction.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Restrictive covenants are enforceable servitudes running with the land where they are (1) in writing, (2) intended to run, (3) touching and concerning the land, and (4) recorded so as to give notice to successors.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Assessments levied under Article VIII became a lien on the lot upon recording of the notice of assessment. The lien is subordinate to a first mortgage recorded earlier in time but superior to subsequent encumbrances.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: A discretionary architectural approval power must be exercised reasonably and in good faith. A denial that states no articulable standard is arbitrary and will not support injunctive relief.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Fines totaling $250 were imposed without the hearing required by the bylaws. A fine imposed in disregard of the association's own procedural requirements is void, without regard to the merits of the underlying violation.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: We reverse the injunction as to the fence and affirm as to the accessory structure. The award of fines is vacated in its entirety.

sections.heading: RIDER 2 — ASSESSMENTS, LIENS AND PRIORITY
sections.text: Annual assessments are levied against each Lot in equal shares and are due on the first day of each fiscal year. Unpaid assessments bear interest at 6 percent per annum and become a lien upon recording of a notice of assessment lien in the Lindenmere County land records. The lien is subordinate to a first mortgage of record predating the notice and superior to all other subsequently recorded encumbrances. The Association shall furnish an estoppel statement of amounts due within 15 days of written request.

sections.heading: RIDER 3 — ENFORCEMENT, FINES AND HEARING RIGHTS
sections.text: Before imposing any fine, the Board shall give the owner written notice of the alleged violation and an opportunity to be heard before the Board or a committee of at least three members who are not officers. Fines shall not exceed $250 per violation nor $2,500 in the aggregate for a continuing violation. A fine imposed without the notice and hearing required by this Rider is void.

sections.heading: RIDER 5 — MAINTENANCE ALLOCATION AND RESERVES
sections.text: The Association maintains the common areas, private drives and stormwater facilities. The owner maintains the Lot and all structures on it, including roofs, windows and exterior doors. The Board shall commission a reserve study not less often than every 20 years and shall fund reserves at not less than 25 percent of the study's recommended annual contribution.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Time of the Essence
sections.text: Time is of the essence as to every obligation stated in this instrument. Where the final day for performance falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday in the State of Kestrel, the period is extended to the next business day.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Attorney's Fees
sections.text: In any action to enforce or construe this instrument, the prevailing party shall recover its reasonable attorney's fees, expert fees and costs, at trial and on appeal. Where the instrument grants fees to one party only, this clause shall be read as reciprocal and shall entitle the other party to fees on the same terms if that party prevails.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Dispute Resolution
sections.text: Before filing suit, a party shall give written notice of the dispute and the parties shall confer in good faith for not fewer than 15 days, and shall thereafter submit the dispute to non-binding mediation before a mediator experienced in real property matters. This clause does not bar an action for injunctive relief to prevent irreparable harm or an action to preserve the status quo.
